_about: Facts both halves of NekoServer use: the runtime builds this file in (common::SHARED), setup reads it (neko_common.SHARED). One copy, so the two can never disagree.

private_settings._about: Root-only files setup writes the outside addresses to (they hold a key): the phone alerts' ntfy address and access token, and the outage monitor's address. Read by Ask Neko to take them out of what the model sees (assist.rs known_secrets).

compose._about: What a Compose file may hold, as `docker compose config --format json` shows it. Anything else (use_api_socket, post_start/pre_stop hooks, secrets, configs, cap_add, a new key Docker adds later) is refused until NekoServer knows what it gives the app. Checked by maintenance.rs valid_model, for setup (check-compose) and the monthly update.

usb_keeps._about: How many of each the weekly copy keeps on the USB drive, the newest ones (backup.rs); the photos and files themselves are never counted or removed. Setup's backups page says these numbers (backup_plan.py offline_row).

left_out._about: The list the weekly copy keeps on an exFAT USB drive of the photos it left out because exFAT can't store their names (backup.rs mirror_on). They are safe on the HDD: a restore from the USB drive (recovery_wizard.py) says so, and never calls them missing copies to repair.

exfat_mount._about: How an exFAT backup drive is mounted: with Linux's own exFAT driver (-i: no mount.exfat helper). Arch's fuse-exfat installs one, and through FUSE the drive's options no longer show who may read it, so every backup refused it as readable by everyone (deep check plan 207). The runtime (backup.rs) and setup (neko_common) take it from here.

media_folders._about: The dashboard's Media folders page (DASHBOARD.md, "Media folders"). The control service (control.rs) checks a change, writes it to `request` in `folder` and starts `unit`, which runs media_locations.py as root: the same code setup uses (existing_media.py). It writes `result`, which the control service hands to the page. `browse_roots`: where the page may look for a folder to pick (drives and shares mounted there), at most `browse_limit` names at a time.
media_folders._progress: A copy into the library at work writes how far it is here (media_locations.CopyProgress): {format, id (the request's), kind, source, files_done, files_total, bytes_done, bytes_total, at}. The control service hands it to the page with the state while the change is at work.
media_folders._folders_per_kind: How many folders of the person's one kind (films, shows or music) may have connected, the one for new downloads counted (existing_media.extras refuses more). `full` says so, on the page and in setup.
media_folders.full: Your {words} have {cap} folders connected already, the most NekoServer connects for one kind. Take one away first, or choose "Copy its files into the library" for this one.
media_folders._slot: Each connected folder's name under library/existing and /data/existing (existing_media.slot_of): the kind, then this. The first folder used where it is is the kind itself ("movies") and a folder only for new downloads is "<kind>-new", as 0.51 named them; more folders get "<kind>-2", "<kind>-3" ... A name is kept for as long as its folder is connected, so the apps' libraries and root folders stay valid. A remove or target request names a folder by it ("library" is the NekoServer library).
media_folders.busy: Already working on a change to your media folders. Wait until it has finished (this page shows it), then try again.
media_folders.away: That drive or share does not answer now. Check that it is switched on and connected, then try again. Nothing was changed.

recovery_menu._about: Choices of the recovery menu (sudo bash install.sh --recover) that messages tell you to pick, as the menu shows them: the menu and every message take them from here.
recovery_menu.check_drive: Check a drive that stopped taking new files

immich_targets._about: Where Immich's containers see the photo library (older and newer image) and the database. Checked by the snapshot's Compose rules (maintenance.rs immich_binds_ok) and by the acceptance check of the running containers (acceptance.py containers).

cats._about: The dashboard's cats (DASHBOARD.md, "The cat"): each mood has a big animation ("home": Home's status cat, the Processes cat, and the stand-in when a small one can't be fetched), a small animation and a still ("pages"). The runtime serves exactly these files, setup installs them.
